title: Cycle Accordion: flexible staffing bands and tranche-first scope prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We propose an "accordion" approach to cycle staffing that defines flexible staffing bands (core / expansion / surge) mapped to tranche ribbons. Each tranche has an attached minimum viable scope and a stretch scope. The playbook codifies when to expand or compress bands, how to cut scope mid-cycle, and a light-weight simulation for headroom accounting. Goals: 1) reduce surprise reprioritization mid-cycle, 2) increase predictability for engineering leads, 3) shorten decision time for scope cuts. This ticket contains the proposed rules, sample allocation heuristics, handoff checklist, and next steps for org sign-off.

decisions: Adopt three-band model: core (committed), expansion (recoverable scope), surge (time-bound, funded by surge pool).
Buffer to reserve: 12% of cycle capacity as default shock lane, adjustable by project risk profile.
Scope cut policy: if projected velocity drops >20% for two consecutive weeks, trigger tranche-first cuts starting from lowest-value stretch items.
Use token-cost variance and infra error-rate as hard constraints for no-new-scope gating for hosted/back-end-affecting work.
